review_notes: I read the whole file and its direct uses in WordRangeWeight, ExpandedScheduleWeight, ExpandedScheduleHistory and ScheduleAtomSystem. I also read the definitions of WordTransferTemplate.state and wordTransferSystem. I did not run Lean. The only simp-interface issue I could support is that the two node-state projection lemmas have no @[simp] attribute, so each caller lists them by hand. The remaining lemmas in the file (the fresh-update product lemmas) have freshness hypotheses, and `reverseCopyLabelMap_product_update` also mentions `reverseCopyLabelMap`. I do not recommend simp for those. The orientation of both node lemmas is sound, and I saw no cycle or competing rule. Remaining uncertainty: a global @[simp] could affect other files that I did not check. The DecidableEq instance on the right-hand side is not fixed by the left-hand side, so it would be synthesized when simp applies the lemma. I did not check whether that matches the instance in every caller's goal.

findings.excerpt:
(wordTransferSystem σ).leftState ((WordTransferTemplate.node d l r).state x) P =
      l.state (Function.update x d.target P)
findings.problem: These are the canonical computation rules for `leftState` and `rightState` on a node state. They rewrite a projection applied to a constructor-built state into a smaller state, so they terminate and normalize in the right direction. They carry no @[simp] attribute, although the sibling definitions in this namespace do use @[simp] for such projection lemmas. Every consumer has to name them by hand in `simp only` lists or `rw`, and two of the callers are separate `simp only` calls. The `rw` call sites in ExpandedScheduleHistory also depend on the exact syntactic form.
findings.proposed_change: Tag both theorems `@[simp]`. They already take `[DecidableEq σ]` as an instance argument, which simp can synthesize for the right-hand side. Then drop `wordTransferLeftState_node, wordTransferRightState_node` from the explicit `simp only` lists in `WordRangeDecoration.weight_eq` and in the expanded-schedule weight proof. If a global attribute is judged too broad, a local `attribute [local simp]` in those two files would achieve the same effect.
findings.benefit: Plain `simp` would reduce the left or right child state of a node template to the child template evaluated at `Function.update x d.target P`. The `simp only` lists at the call sites would no longer need to be kept in sync with these lemma names.
